parsed.rationale: All three types — `HSBColor` (package `ColorPalette`, `HSBColor.swift:31`), `HSBOffset` (`ThemeColors.swift:198`), and `AccentColor` (`ThemeColors.swift:62`) — share the initializer label `init(hue:saturation:brightness:)`, but the structural evidence shows `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, meaning no field-level overlap was confirmed. `HSBOffset` encodes a relative delta in HSB space, which is a semantically distinct concept from the concrete color types `HSBColor` and `AccentColor`; the initializer label coincidence is a natural consequence of the HSB parameter domain, not a sign of shared logic. Introducing a protocol with a default implementation would either force a semantically incorrect body onto `HSBOffset` or produce a vacuous protocol that adds indirection without eliminating any real duplication.
